title: Rigveda 4.52: To Usas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.52: To Usas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.52 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Usas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 311v-312r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.52.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 311v
translation.original_text:
1prati̱ ṣyā sū̱narī̱ janī̍ vyu̱cchantī̱ pari̱ svasu̍ḥ | di̱vo a̍darśi duhi̱tā ||
2aśve̍va ci̱trāru̍ṣī mā̱tā gavā̍m ṛ̱tāva̍rī | sakhā̍bhūd a̱śvino̍r u̱ṣāḥ ||
3u̱ta sakhā̍sy a̱śvino̍r u̱ta mā̱tā gavā̍m asi | u̱toṣo̱ vasva̍ īśiṣe ||
4yā̱va̱yaddve̍ṣasaṁ tvā ciki̱tvit sū̍nṛtāvari | prati̱ stomai̍r abhutsmahi ||
translation.text:
1THIS Lady, giver of delight, after her Sister shining forth, Daughter of Heaven, hath shown herself.-
2Unfailing, Mother of the Kine, in colour like a bright red mare, The Dawn became the Aṣvins' Friend.
3Yea, and thou art the Aṣvins' Friend, the Mother of the Kine art thou: O Dawn thou rulest over wealth.
4Thinking of thee, O joyous One, as her who driveth hate away, We woke to meet thee with our lauds.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 311v (numbered 120v by the scribe) (OPenn image 312, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.51.10 ‹-syāma›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 312r (numbered 121r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.52.5 ‹ā uṣāḥ aprāḥ uru›. Verses 4.52.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1prati | syā | sūnarī | janī | vi-ucchantī | pari | svasuḥ | divaḥ | adarśi | duhitā
2aśvāiva | citrā | aruṣī | mātā | gavām | ṛta-varī | sakhā | abhūt | aśvinoḥ | uṣāḥ
3uta | sakhā | asi | aśvinoḥ | uta | mātā | gavām | asi | uta | uṣaḥ | vasvaḥ | īśiṣe
4yāvayat-dveṣasam | tvā | cikitvit | sūnṛtāvari | prati | stomaiḥ | abhutsmahi

translation.original_ref: RV 4.52.5-7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 312r
translation.original_text:
5prati̍ bha̱drā a̍dṛkṣata̱ gavā̱ṁ sargā̱ na ra̱śmaya̍ḥ | oṣā a̍prā u̱ru jraya̍ḥ ||
6ā̱pa̱pruṣī̍ vibhāvari̱ vy ā̍va̱r jyoti̍ṣā̱ tama̍ḥ | uṣo̱ anu̍ sva̱dhām a̍va ||
7ā dyāṁ ta̍noṣi ra̱śmibhi̱r āntari̍kṣam u̱ru pri̱yam | uṣa̍ḥ śu̱kreṇa̍ śo̱ciṣā̍ ||
translation.text:
5Our eyes behold thy blessed rays like troops of cattle loosed to feed. Dawn hath filled full the wide expanse.
6When thou hast filled it, Fulgent One! thou layest bare the gloom with light. After thy nature aid us, Dawn.
7Thou overspreadest heaven with rays, the dear wide region of mid-air. With thy bright shining lustre, Dawn.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 312r (numbered 121r by the scribe) (OPenn image 312, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.52.5 ‹ā uṣāḥ aprāḥ uru›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 312v (numbered 121v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.53.3 ‹devaḥ kṛṇute svāya dharmaṇe›. Verses 4.52.5-7 end on this page; 4.52.5 begins on fol. 311v (numbered 120v by the scribe).

5prati | bhadrāḥ | adṛkṣata | gavām | sargāḥ | na | raśmayaḥ | ā | uṣāḥ | aprāḥ | uru | jrayaḥ
6āpapruṣī | vibhāvari | vi | āvaḥ | jyotiṣā | tamaḥ | uṣaḥ | anu | svadhām | ava
7ā | dyām | tanoṣi | raśmi-bhiḥ | ā | antarikṣam | uru | priyam | uṣaḥ | śukreṇa | śociṣā
